# TA_PUBGOODS PLAYBOOK

**On contribution strategy:**
When deciding how much to contribute to the envelope, I will contribute conservatively once I establish a lead. The Nash equilibrium is to free-ride (contribute 0), and while I started with moderate contributions to signal willingness to cooperate, I should shift toward minimizing contributions as soon as I'm ahead, since the equal split of the pot means my relative advantage grows by keeping tokens out of circulation.

**On declaration:**
When filing my receipt, I will always declare the exact amount in my envelope. The game requires receipts to match envelope contents exactly, and honest declaration avoids any penalties or complications. There is no strategic advantage to misrepresenting what I actually contributed.

**On early-game positioning:**
When I don't yet know opponents' strategies, I will start with a moderate contribution (around 10) to test the waters and appear reasonably cooperative without sacrificing too much.

**On late-game execution:**
When I have a lead with few rounds remaining, I will reduce my contributions substantially to protect my advantage. Since payoffs are split equally among all players regardless of my contribution amount, lower contributions directly maximize my final score relative to others.

**On the pattern I observed:**
When opponents consistently contribute around 10 tokens while I drift lower, this creates a widening gap in my favor. I should lean into this asymmetry rather than try to match their contributions.

**What did not work:**
My initial assumption that "moderate contribution leaves room to adapt" was imprecise. What actually worked was recognizing early that a lead could be secured and then systematically reducing contributions to maintain it. I should not second-guess the free-riding strategy once the game state allows it.
